key_insight: A tree-based adaptive finite-element level-set transport method refines only near the moving interface, keeping accuracy high while cutting cost.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical, mesh-compatible way to track evolving two-phase flow interfaces on structured or unstructured 2D/3D grids.
method: Dynamic local refinement and coarsening on a hierarchical mesh
Marker-driven interface prediction with backward characteristic tracing
Multilevel marker and point-location search across refinement levels
evidence_signal: The method was tested on severe interface deformations in 2D and 3D across quadrilateral, simplicial, wedge, and hexahedral meshes, showing accuracy comparable to uniform grids at much lower cost.
watch_item: Aggressive adaptivity can complicate implementation, especially robust point-location, data management, and conservation control near refinement boundaries.
paper_title: An Adaptive Finite Element Method for Marker-Driven Level-Set Transport on Hierarchical Meshes
